2024-03/A0073-H.text: Costco Is Cutting Prices on Several Items, Executive Says

2024-03/A0077-S01.text: (Reuters) -Costco's shares closed down 7.6% on Friday for its worst day since May 2022 after the membership-only retail chain missed second-quarter revenue expectations and signaled a negative impact from lower gasoline prices.

2024-03/A0077-S02.text: "Gasoline price deflation negatively impacted total reported comp sales ... the average worldwide selling price per gallon of gas was down approximately 3.5% versus last year," Costco's outgoing CFO Richard Gallanti said.

2024-03/A0081-S01.text: On the earnings front, Costco (COST) shares are under pressure after the retailer reported second quarter revenue that missed expectations.

2024-05/A0009-S01.text: Costco's total revenue was $58.52 billion for the quarter ended May 12, compared with analysts' average estimate of $58.07 billion, according to LSEG data.

2024-05/A0009-S02.text: Costco's total comparable sales rose 6.5% on an adjusted basis in the quarter, compared to a 3.5% rise last year.

2024-05/A0009-S03.text: The company's ecommerce comparable sales rose 20.7%, led by gold and silver bullion, gift cards and appliances.

2024-05/A0010-S01.text: On Thursday afternoon, the company reported net sales of $58.52 billion, compared to estimates of $57.98 billion.

2024-05/A0010-S02.text: Same-store sales, excluding fuel, jumped 6.5%, led by its growing international business (up 8.5%), Canada (up 7.4%), and the US (up 6%).

2024-06/A0041-S02.text: There is one card that Costco could play that could drive up some bullishness in the near term, potentially pushing it to a $1,000 valuation, and that's a hike to its membership fees.

2024-06/A0043-S03.text: Amid surges in profits, Costco warned consumers that they may have to pay a heftier fee in the future for the retailer's annual membership.

2024-06/A0060-S01.text: The massive warehouse store operator just reported revenue of $58.5 billion (up 9% year over year) and diluted earnings per share of $3.78 (up 29%) that easily beat Wall Street consensus analyst estimates.

2024-06/A0060-S02.text: In the latest fiscal quarter (Q3 2024, ended May 12), same-store sales increased 6.6%.

2024-06/A0067-S01.text: In their recent earnings report, both Target and Walmart noted a pullback in discretionary spending, while Costco's value and unique deals have given way to more discretionary spending and a larger market share.

2024-06/A0067-S02.text: For the quarter ended on May 12, Costco recorded revenue grew 9% YoY to $58.52 billion, earning $3.78 per share.

2024-06/A0067-S03.text: Costco is waiting for the right time to raise membership prices. Throughout most of its history, Costco has been raising its membership prices every five years on average, but it's now been nearly seven years since its last price hike and Costco is still keeping them steady.

2024-07/A0073-S01.text: The leading warehouse club operator announced this week that it is boosting its annual membership prices by 8% in September.

2024-07/A0073-S03.text: However, that $3.3 billion in membership fees accounts for more than half of the $6.2 billion in operating profit that it has served up in that time.

2024-07/A0076-S01.text: The bank said in a Thursday note that Costco's first membership hike in seven years will give investors greater earnings visibility into 2026.

2024-07/A0078-S02.text: Starting Sept. 1, fees will increase to $65 for individuals and $130 for executive memberships, up from $60 and $120, representing an 8% hike for both categories.

2024-07/A0080-S01.text: The retailer is raising membership fees by $5 to $65 a year in the US and Canada, Costco announced Wednesday.

2024-07/A0081-S02.text: The higher fees will go into effect from Sept. 1., and are expected to boost Costco's revenue.

2024-07/A0083-S01.text: (Reuters) - Costco Wholesale said on Wednesday it would hike annual membership fees for the first time in seven years for its U.S. and Canada customers, effective Sept. 1.

2024-09/A0016-S02.text: The US and Canada renewal rate slightly decreased to 92.9%, impacted by lower renewal rates from a digital promotion cohort.

2024-09/A0018-S01.text: (Reuters) -Costco Wholesale missed market expectations for fourth-quarter revenue on Thursday hurt by cautious consumer spending on pricier items at its membership-only stores and lower gasoline prices.

2024-09/A0018-S02.text: The membership warehouse retailer's same-store sales also took a hit from lower gasoline prices. They grew 5.4% in the reported period ended Sept. 1, compared with a 6.6% rise in the third quarter.

2024-09/A0022-S01.text: But the company posted a slight miss on revenue, with $79.7 billion, compared to expectations of $79.96 billion.

2024-12/A0002-S01.text: E-commerce sales rose 13% in the quarter compared with the year-ago period. The company is gaining market share by shipping big and bulky items, CEO Ron Vachris said on the company's earnings call, and it hit nearly 1 million deliveries in the quarter, which was a new record.

2024-12/A0002-S03.text: It ended the quarter with 77.4 million paid household members, an approximately 8% year over year increase, or 138.8 million cardholders.

2024-12/A0012-S01.text: Total company comparable sales growth, excluding fuel: 7.2% versus 6.26%

2024-12/A0015-S01.text: Analysts expect Costco will report a revenue bump of roughly 7% to $62.1 billion compared to $57.8 billion at the same time last year, according to estimates compiled by Visible Alpha.

2024-12/A0015-S02.text: However, analysts remained bullish following the monthly data as JPM analysts said Costco's "core trends" are "ahead of expectations and quite robust," while Oppenheimer analysts raised the idea of a future stock split as a potential "positive catalyst" for Costco shares.
